The test image shows a young soybean seedling that has collapsed at the soil line, with severely wilted/drooping leaves that are yellowing and browning. The plant is collapsing near the soil surface in sandy soil — classic damping off pattern.

Top candidates:
- **Pythium_damping_off**: water-soaked lesions on hypocotyl, brown soft rot, collapse at soil line
- **Rhizoctonia**: also causes damping off with reddish-brown stem lesions (wire stem)
- **Phytophthora**: yellowing/wilting but more in mature plants

Let me view the Pythium reference image.

The reference Pythium image shows early pre-emergence damping off (rotted brown hypocotyl at seedling stage). The test image shows a more developed seedling that has completely collapsed at the soil line — post-emergence damping off. The overall collapse pattern, wilting, and failure at the soil surface matches Pythium damping off (post-emergence stage), which describes exactly "water-soaked lesions on hypocotyl that turn into brown soft rot, with rotted roots allowing diseased plants to be easily pulled from soil."

The plant in the test image has the characteristic "melting off" appearance — stem has rotted at/near the soil line causing total collapse of the above-ground portion. This is distinct from Rhizoctonia (which tends to leave a more defined wire-stem lesion) or Phytophthora (which shows chocolate-brown stem discoloration moving upward in larger plants).
